h: Rides, roof gardens and a walk to the falls
p: One feature that surprises first-time visitors to New Lanark is the Annie McLeod Experience, a gentle dark ride where you're carried through the story of the village through the eyes of a young mill girl. It's a great way to get younger children engaged before they explore the rest of the site. Afterwards, head up to the roof garden on top of one of the mills for views over the river, the village and the wooded slopes of the gorge.

Robert Owen's House is another highlight, showing how the famous manager lived alongside the workers he wanted to help. The village store and the mill workers' homes are fascinating too, and the restored schoolhouse helps explain why Owen was so ahead of his time in believing that children should be educated rather than sent to work.

The walk to the Falls of Clyde is a must if the weather allows. It follows the river through a Scottish Wildlife Trust reserve up to Corra Linn, the most impressive of the falls, and keen eyes may spot peregrine falcons, which have nested in the gorge. Water levels vary, so the falls are at their most dramatic after rain, but the paths can be slippery, so take care with young children.

New Lanark also has a hotel, cafés and shops in the village, so it's easy to make a weekend of it. Lanark itself has a long history as a royal burgh, and the Clyde Valley around it is dotted with orchards, garden centres and country lanes that make for a relaxed drive back.
